data.why: The landing dashboard, leaderboard and examples pages read from a SQLite DB that a fresh clone doesn't have (it is normally built by a weekly backfill against RCSB/AlphaFold DB, which this sandbox cannot reach at runtime); an install step seeds that DB with the 9 structures README already documents (metrics transcribed from the README's own published case studies: the Artemis positive control plus the 8 curated failure deep-dives spanning amyloid, conformational, assembly and context-fragment errors), and rebuilds the weekly-examples and Calculate-autocomplete indexes from them so every page has real, internally-consistent content without any network access.

goals: Decide whether AlphaFold's blind prediction for a given human PDB entry matches the deposited experimental structure, and by how much (TM-score, lDDT, Cα-RMSD)
Find which human protein folds AlphaFold gets systematically wrong, ranked by confidence-weighted error (the FRAUD leaderboard)
Audit whether AlphaFold's self-reported confidence (pLDDT) is calibrated to its actual accuracy, or whether it is confidently wrong
Distinguish different failure mechanisms -- misfold, wrong conformational state, wrong complex/assembly context, or amyloid polymorph -- across the curated deep-dive examples
Browse the archive of PDB release weeks to see how often newly deposited structures catch AlphaFold overconfident

review.summary: The tree captures AlphaFraud's purpose well: it covers checking one structure, surveying confident failures, ranking them, auditing calibration, sorting failure mechanisms and browsing weekly batches, and the cited screens hold up on inspection. Before filing it needs moderate fixes: move an offline-only task and an ops-only task out, regroup the calibration phase around the dumbbell chart, correct the archive dropdown claim, and add two missing features (the per-entry record and the explainer panel).
